summary.one_liner: bat is a cat(1) clone written for the terminal that adds syntax highlighting, Git change markers, and automatic paging.
summary.what_it_does: Displays one or more files in the terminal with syntax highlighting for many programming and markup languages. When run in an interactive terminal it shows Git modification markers against the index and can show non-printable characters via -A. Output is sent to a pager such as less when it exceeds one screen, and falls back to plain cat-like output when piped or redirected. It reads stdin, and can be used as a previewer for fzf or as a colorizing pager for man and --help output. Themes, output style components (numbers, grid, header, changes, snip), and custom syntaxes or themes (.sublime-syntax and .tmTheme) can be configured via a config file or environment variables.
use_cases: view source code with syntax highlighting in the terminal
replace cat with a colorized version
show git changes alongside file contents
notable: Git integration marks modified lines against the index in the sidebar
Automatically pipes to a pager only when output is larger than one screen
Acts as a plain drop-in cat when output is not a terminal
Supports custom Sublime .sublime-syntax languages and .tmTheme themes via a cache build step
Ships a manpage syntax and a help syntax for colorizing --help output
caveats: Requires Rust 1.79.0 or higher to build from source
Windows needs the Visual C++ Redistributable and a separate less binary for good paging
On some older Debian/Ubuntu releases the executable is named batcat
Newer .sublime-color-scheme theme files are not supported
